title: 3-DOF arm with a gripper
about: 3 revolute joints (yaw, shoulder, elbow) and 2 prismatic fingers. The right finger uses <mimic>, so one slider moves both.

title: 6-DOF industrial arm
about: Six revolute joints named like a Universal Robots arm, ending in an empty tool0 frame where a gripper would be fixed.

real.title: Universal Robots ROS 2 description (UR3 to UR30)

title: Quadcopter
about: One body, four fixed motors and four propellers on continuous joints. In flight, the body's position comes from an odom → base_link transform, not from the URDF.

real.title: sjtu_drone ROS 2 quadcopter simulator (GPLv3: link, don't copy)

title: Chiku: 2-wheeled mobile robot
about: A differential-drive robot: two continuous wheel joints, a fixed caster and an optional lidar (xacro arg use_lidar).

title: Chiku with mesh files
about: The same robot drawn with STL meshes (in millimetres, so scale 0.001) and simple boxes and cylinders for collision.

title: 4-legged robot
about: 12 revolute joints: hip, thigh and calf on each leg, written once as a leg macro and used four times.

title: 6-legged spider robot
about: 18 revolute joints. Each leg is the same macro; only the yaw angle of its first joint changes (0°, 60° … 300°).

real.title: PhantomX hexapod description (ROS 1, good porting exercise)

title: Humanoid
about: 21 revolute joints: waist, neck pan and tilt, 3 per arm and 6 per leg. Arms and legs are macros with a left/right sign.

title: Hybrid: mobile manipulator
about: Chiku's base plus the 3-DOF arm, joined by one fixed joint. The arm comes from the same macro file as the arm robot, with prefix arm_.

title: Hybrid: legged manipulator
about: The 4-legged robot carrying the arm: 12 leg joints + 3 arm joints + a gripper, all from reused macros.

title: Car-like (Ackermann) robot
about: Two front steering joints (revolute, ±0.6 rad) and four wheels (continuous), like a car.

title: Mecanum (omnidirectional) robot
about: Four continuous wheels; the tilted bars show the 45° rollers that let it drive sideways.

title: Universal Robots UR5e
about: 6-DOF collaborative arm, 5 kg payload, 850 mm reach. The official ROS 2 description (ur_type:=ur5e) with its DAE meshes.

real.connection: Ethernet (set robot_ip; install the External Control URCap and press play on the teach pendant)
real.launch: ros2 launch ur_robot_driver ur_control.launch.py ur_type:=ur5e robot_ip:=192.168.56.101 launch_rviz:=false

title: Franka Research 3 with Franka Hand
about: 7-DOF torque-controlled research arm with the two-finger Franka Hand (hand:=true). The second finger is a mimic joint.

real.driver: franka_ros2 (jazzy branch, source build; PREEMPT_RT kernel, activate FCI in Desk)
real.install: git clone -b jazzy https://github.com/frankarobotics/franka_ros2.git src/franka_ros2 && vcs import src < src/franka_ros2/dependency.repos --recursive --skip-existing && rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro jazzy -y && colcon build --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
real.connection: Ethernet to the Control box (default robot_ip 172.16.0.3)

title: Kinova Gen3 7-DOF with vision module
about: 7-DOF ultra-light arm with the wrist RGB-D vision module (dof:=7 vision:=true). sim.launch.py adds the wrist camera as a Gazebo rgbd_camera and position controllers on joints 2, 4 and 6: move them with ros2 topic pub /joint_2/cmd_pos std_msgs/msg/Float64 "{data: 1.0}".

real.connection: Ethernet, factory IP 192.168.1.10 (set the PC to 192.168.1.11/24)
real.launch: ros2 launch kortex_bringup gen3.launch.py robot_ip:=192.168.1.10 dof:=7 launch_rviz:=false

title: UFACTORY xArm 6
about: 6-DOF arm from the official xarm_ros2 description (dof:=6 robot_type:=xarm).

real.install: git clone https://github.com/xArm-Developer/xarm_ros2.git --recursive -b jazzy src/xarm_ros2 && rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro jazzy -y && colcon build
real.connection: Ethernet (the IP printed on the control box, e.g. 192.168.1.117)

title: UFACTORY Lite 6
about: Low-cost 6-DOF desktop arm (robot_type:=lite).

real.install: git clone https://github.com/xArm-Developer/xarm_ros2.git --recursive -b jazzy src/xarm_ros2 && rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro jazzy -y && colcon build

title: Dobot CR5
about: 6-DOF collaborative arm, 5 kg payload, from Dobot's ROS 2 V4 driver package.

real.driver: DOBOT_6Axis_ROS2_V4 (jazzy branch; controller in TCP/IP remote mode)
real.install: git clone -b jazzy https://github.com/Dobot-Arm/DOBOT_6Axis_ROS2_V4.git src/DOBOT_6Axis_ROS2_V4 && rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro jazzy -y && colcon build

title: Dobot Magician
about: 4-axis desktop arm for education. Its parallel links are modelled with mimic joints, so only the motor joints have sliders.

real.driver: magician_ros2 (Humble only upstream: it has no FollowJointTrajectory, so MoveIt plans and you send the result with its /PTP_action)
real.install: git clone https://github.com/jkaniuka/magician_ros2.git src/magician_ros2 && pip install -r src/magician_ros2/requirements.txt && colcon build

title: SO-101 (LeRobot arm)
about: Open-source 5-DOF + gripper arm used with LeRobot for imitation learning.

real.driver: feetech_ros2_driver (ros2_control hardware for the STS3215 servos)
real.connection: USB serial /dev/ttyACM0 (sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER; calibrate the motors with LeRobot first)

title: Trossen WidowX 250 6DOF
about: 6-DOF research arm with a gripper. Every frame has the robot name as a prefix (wx250s/...), as the Interbotix packages publish them.

real.driver: interbotix_ros_manipulators + interbotix_ros_core (jazzy branches, source build; vendor-tested on Humble)
real.install: git clone -b jazzy https://github.com/Interbotix/interbotix_ros_core.git src/interbotix_ros_core && git clone -b jazzy https://github.com/Interbotix/interbotix_ros_manipulators.git src/interbotix_ros_manipulators && git clone -b jazzy https://github.com/Interbotix/interbotix_ros_toolboxes.git src/interbotix_ros_toolboxes && rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro jazzy -y && colcon build

title: ABB IRB 120
about: ABB's smallest industrial arm (3 kg, 580 mm). ROS-Industrial support package: base_link to tool0 with the joint limits of the controller.

real.driver: abb_ros2 (rolling branch, source build; the controller needs the EGM option)
real.install: git clone https://github.com/PickNikRobotics/abb_ros2.git src/abb_ros2 && vcs import src < src/abb_ros2/abb.repos && rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro jazzy -y && colcon build
real.connection: Ethernet (RWS at the controller IP, EGM UDP port 6511)

title: KUKA KR 6 R900 sixx (Agilus)
about: Fast 6 kg industrial arm. ROS-Industrial support package with base_link, flange and tool0 frames.

real.connection: Ethernet, UDP RSI (client_port 59152; KR C4 with the RSI option; RT kernel recommended)
real.launch: ros2 launch kuka_rsi_driver startup.launch.py robot_family:=agilus robot_model:=kr6_r900_2 client_ip:=<PC_IP>   (then: ros2 lifecycle set robot_manager configure && ros2 lifecycle set robot_manager activate)

title: FANUC LR Mate 200iD
about: Compact 7 kg industrial arm. ROS-Industrial support package (flange and tool0 frames, controller joint limits).

real.driver: FANUC fanuc_driver (main = jazzy; controller options J519 Stream Motion + R912 Remote Motion)
real.install: sudo apt install git-lfs && git lfs install && git clone https://github.com/FANUC-CORPORATION/fanuc_description.git src/fanuc_description && git clone --branch main --recurse-submodules https://github.com/FANUC-CORPORATION/fanuc_driver.git src/fanuc_driver && rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src --rosdistro jazzy -y && colcon build
real.launch: ros2 launch fanuc_hardware_interface fanuc_physical_control.launch.py robot_series:=lrmate robot_model:=lrmate200id robot_ip:=192.168.1.100

title: TurtleBot3 Waffle
about: Differential-drive research robot with an LDS-01 360° lidar, an RGB camera and an IMU. sim.launch.py runs it in Gazebo: scan, camera image, IMU and odometry appear in RViz; drive it with teleop_twist_keyboard.

title: TurtleBot3 Burger
about: The small TurtleBot3: two wheels, an LDS-01 lidar and an IMU. sim.launch.py runs it in Gazebo.

title: AgileX Scout V2
about: Four-wheel skid-steer outdoor platform. In this description the wheel joints are fixed, so there are no sliders.

sim.note: AgileX Scout V2: skid steering with four wheels (DiffDrive with two wheels per side). The real base (scout_base over CAN) takes geometry_msgs/Twist on /cmd_vel.

title: Unitree Go2
about: 12-joint quadruped with the L1 4D lidar, a front camera and an IMU. sim.launch.py adds them as Gazebo sensors. Without a walking controller the robot only stands (here it is held in place).

velocity.note: Unitree Go2 walks with Unitree's own locomotion controller (community Gazebo packages use CHAMP).

title: Unitree G1 humanoid (29 DOF)
about: 1.3 m humanoid with a Livox MID-360 lidar, an Intel RealSense D435 and IMUs. sim.launch.py adds the lidar, the RGB-D camera and the pelvis IMU as Gazebo sensors.

velocity.note: Unitree G1 balances and walks with Unitree's learned locomotion policy.

title: Unitree H1 humanoid
about: 1.8 m full-size humanoid with a MID-360 lidar and a RealSense D435 in the head.

velocity.note: Unitree H1 walks with Unitree's own locomotion controller.

title: Boston Dynamics Spot
about: 12-joint quadruped with its OBJ meshes and textures (materials come from the .mtl file).

velocity.note: Boston Dynamics Spot walks with its own on-board controller; spot_driver sends it geometry_msgs/Twist on cmd_vel. Here VelocityControl moves the standing body the same way.

title: Bitcraze Crazyflie 2.1
about: 27 g nano quadcopter used in Crazyswarm2 drone swarms. One link with the whole frame as a mesh; in flight its pose comes from TF (world -> cf).

velocity.note: Bitcraze Crazyflie 2.1: crazyswarm2 flies the real one (cmd_vel_legacy / cmd_hover / go_to). Here VelocityControl flies the body in 3-D: i , j l move, t / b climb and descend.
